sections.title: Operating Principles
paras: Deepgram is a research company that productizes as fast as possible. Four Operating Principles shape how we think, decide, and work together:
We look for people who already work this way, and these principles shape how we grow and evaluate our team.
bullets: Compress before you communicate. You think it through first, then lead with the bottom line.
Resist entropy. You question what already exists before adding more process or tools.
Solve the category. You fix recurring problems at the source, not one case at a time.
Work at the frontier. You go after problems no one has solved yet.

sections.title: AI-First by Default
paras: We build AI that millions of people talk to, and we run the company the same way. AI is how we centralize work here, and is core to how we operate.
That means more than using the tools. We expect you to:

We judge AI by what it helps you deliver and whether you stand behind the result, not by how often you use it. In interviews, expect to walk us through a workflow you built and where you drew the line between AI and your own judgment.
bullets: Build, not just use. Design your own workflows and agents, and use AI to remove whole categories of work instead of doing the same work faster.
Own the output. AI can speed up the work. It doesn’t make anyone less accountable for it. You understand, verify, and stand behind everything you share, including what an agent produces for you.
Spend the time you get back at the frontier. The capacity AI creates goes toward problems no one has solved yet.
Keep pace. Models and tools change every month, and so will your work. You adopt what’s new quickly and drop what no longer earns its place.

To thrive in this role, you’ll need experience working with developers and a technical knowledge of developer tools. You’ll need to know how to work with the developer community and understand the lifecycle of software development, the software supply chain and how AI agents are safely orchestrated and deployed with sandboxes. You’ll need a relentless drive to try new things, and an eye for detail. Your long-term success will depend on your ability to own the product roadmap and collaborate with the developer community, and scale our services. Most importantly, you’ll need to be okay with taking ownership of big objectives with big goals, working with a cross-functional team, and maintaining a bias for action.

ashby:forus:34d39cf3-3ec0-4b11-9284-73c6.summary:
Forus is building an AI-powered network that connects doctors, pharmacies, payers, and biopharma to accelerate new science to patients.

Our platform automates the complexity between a doctor prescribing a medicine and a patient starting treatment, including insurance coverage, financial assistance, and supply chain navigation. We provide this support free to doctors and patients, helping them get life-changing medicine faster, cheaper, and easier. The resulting network enables biopharma companies to design better research, launch new drugs more effectively, and invest in harder-to-treat conditions.

Forus has exceptional product-market fit and is growing rapidly through organic adoption:

sections.title: About the role
paras:
As a Strategic Product Manager at Forus, you will take on some of the company’s most important and ambiguous product problems before they have established teams, roadmaps, or obvious solutions. Your work may include building internal AI and automation products, creating new operational capabilities, developing the first version of a product for a new customer category, or incubating an entirely new business line. Some initiatives will become permanent product areas; others may be handed to an existing team once the problem has been understood and the initial solution is working.

You will operate as a technical product generalist, moving fluidly between product strategy, software, data, operations, and commercial considerations. You will be expected to identify the real constraint, develop a practical solution, build or prototype where useful, and lead execution until the initiative produces a measurable outcome. Depending on the problem, you may work through a dedicated engineering team, lead a broader cross-functional group, or execute significant portions of the work yourself.

This is a demanding role, with a high level of autonomy and responsibility. You will be expected to "act like an owner" and commit yourself to Forus' success. If you are low-ego, hungry to learn, and excited about intense, impactful work that drives both company growth and accelerated career progression, we want to hear from you.

sections.title: If you join, you will:

You’ll design how our agents listen, interpret, respond, and guide patients through real healthcare workflows. From conversation structure and language choices to tool use, transfers, and recovery when something goes wrong, you’ll turn complex requirements into conversations that feel natural and accomplish the task.

This is a hands-on building role. You’ll create prompts, conversation flows, and agent configurations yourself, then use simulations and real chats with the agent to understand where conversations break down and improve them. You’ll work closely with Engineering and Customer Delivery Product Managers to make sure the experience holds up in…

sections.title: Design and build production-ready agents
bullets: Own agent architecture and configuration, including prompts, intents, conversation flows, tool calls, extensions, transfer protocols, and retrieval-augmented knowledge bases.
Lead technical discovery to translate customer business processes, rules, exceptions, and handoffs into agent behavior.
Build agents that handle real healthcare complexity, including scheduling logic, patient context, EHR data, and practice-specific requirements.
Partner with Engineering on integrations, new features, and end-to-end testing, translating integration constraints into agent design decisions.
Assess technical feasibility and help the Customer Delivery PM understand implementation effort and tradeoffs before scope and timelines are committed.

sections.title: Own agent quality and production performance
bullets: Author evaluations, tags, and simulation scenarios that test expected behavior, edge cases, and failure modes.
Build and run simulation suites, review results, and own internal agent quality before customer demos and testing.
Peer-review other builders’ agents and take accountability for the technical approvals you provide.
Diagnose issues during soft launch and the initial period after go-live, using live conversations, evaluations, and customer feedback to guide improvements.
Decide when an issue requires a targeted fix and when the agent needs to be re-architected.

sections.title: Guide agents as they evolve

Remain the architectural owner of the agents you build, advising on changes that affect their structure and behavior.
Review Agent Technician pull requests and lead refactors that require deeper architectural work.
Assess whether expansion requests can reuse existing features or require new capabilities.
Turn patterns across deployments into reusable components and patterns so that future agents are built faster

Strong understanding of conversation structure, turn-taking, intent recognition, ambiguity, clarification, and recovery when an interaction goes off track.
Hands-on prompt engineering skills and the ability to translate customer workflows into agent instructions, conversation flows, and decision logic.
Ability to review calls and transcripts, identify patterns in conversational failures, and turn those findings into concrete improvements.
Technical fluency with agent-building platforms, tool calls, APIs, and integrations, including how system constraints affect the conversation.
Strong ownership and the ability to work across customer-facing and engineering teams in a fast-moving environment.

incident.io is the AI software reliability platform trusted by engineering teams at Notion, Linear, Ramp and 2,000+ companies who can't afford downtime.

The stakes are real, the talent is insane, and somehow it's a genuinely lovely place to work. We all pull our weight, go the extra mile, and put in the bit of magic most companies don't have time for, all while having fun and never taking ourselves too seriously.

We've raised $100+ million from Index Ventures, Insight Partners, and Point Nine, and we're growing fast. There's never been a better time to join.

sections.title: The role in one line
paras: Solutions Engineering at incident.io is where the product meets the moment it's built for - you're the person who turns "we'll see" into "oh, this actually works," proving live that we hold up exactly when it matters most.

sections.title: What that looks like day to day
paras: As a Solutions Engineer at incident.io , you're the technical voice in the room from first discovery call through to close, partnering closely with our Account Executives across the commercial segment. You'll be in front of some of the most exciting companies we sell into, running demos that need to hold up under real scrutiny - because the people you're presenting to have felt what it's like when tools fall over during an incident, and they're not going to be won over by a slide deck.

This function is still being built, which means there's real room to bring your own ideas to the table and help shape how Solutions Engineering works at incident, not just execute a playbook someone else wrote. You'll report into our Solutions Engineering Manager - our founding Solutions Engineer - and the wider segment sits under our co-founder and Field CTO, so you'll have direct access to people who've done this from the ground up.

You'll occasionally work alongside our TSEs and Product team, though that's the exception rather than the rule - most of your time is spent partnered tightly with AEs, going deep on a prospect's world before you ever get in the room.

sections.title: Who you are
bullets: You've been a Solutions Engineer before, and you've stood in front of senior stakeholders and run demos that actually landed - not just clicked through slides.
You have a genuine interest in code and solving hard technical problems - not because a job spec told you to, but because you can't help yourself.
You operate with high ownership - if something needs sorting, you don't wait to be asked.
You want to know this product inside and out, not just enough to get through a demo.
When a technical objection comes up and you don't have the answer, it bugs you until you find it - that's when you're at your best.
Thriving under pressure is your normal, not your exception - the moments when everything's on the line are the moments you show up hardest.
You want to build something, not just execute someone else's playbook - this function is still taking shape, and you want a say in what it becomes.

sections.title: Supporting you
paras: We work hard and we think life outside work matters just as much. Our benefits pack is built to support both.
bullets: Market-leading private medical insurance. The proper kind, so you're never weighing up your health against a bill.
Competitive PTO. Showing up at your best requires switching off, and we make sure you have time to do that.
First Friday of every month off. Yes, seriously.
Enhanced 401k. We put real money in, because future-you deserves better than an afterthought.
Meaningful equity. We're rapidly scaling, and everyone who helps shape the outcome should share in it.
Unlimited AI spend. For everyone, not just engineers. We're all-in on AI across the company, and we expect you to be too.
Generous parental leave. The early days with a new baby matter more than anything we're doing here, and we want you to be present for them.
Two budgets that have your back. $1000 to invest in your setup, $500 a year to invest in yourself.

ashby:meter:67bd0f98-f604-4038-9bea-846b.summary:
The internet runs the world. Every purchase you make, video call you join, it is all packets flowing through networks. But those networks have not changed for decades. They are brittle, complex, and surprisingly hard to set up in an enterprise space.

We started Meter to build better networks. We had to build everything from the ground up: designing and building our own enterprise hardware, intuitive software, and streamlined operations to deliver great outcomes for our customers. Today, we build and deploy these networks at scale. Ambitious companies and enduring institutions like Bridgewater, Lyft, and Reddit rely on Meter to keep their thousands of employees and locations online and productive.

sections.title: This role is critical to Meter's success
paras: Meter’s next phase of growth depends not just on winning new customers, but on consistently proving that we can replace decades of legacy infrastructure. Every interaction shapes whether a customer doubles down on us or falls back to the status quo. As an early member of the team, you’ll help define the Customer Success function and directly influence how we scale.

We deploy networks across a wide range of customers, from healthcare clinics and school districts to logistics hubs, retail chains, and professional services firms. Customer Success is responsible for delivering a consistent, high-quality experience across this diversity, ensuring that Meter becomes a trusted, long-term connectivity partner.

sections.title: What Success Looks Like
bullets: For a product launch, you know which customers to call first. You help build the early access list, pressure-test major assumptions and shape the final offering.
You know the expansion potential of every account in your book of business, and your quarterly pipeline forecast lands within 20% of actual attainment.
When a customer moves with Meter, the transition feels choreographed. You’re looped in early, bandwidth and hardware are right-sized, and a turnkey network awaits the team in their new space.

You lay the groundwork for Meter’s commercial advantages to compound over time. Every customer who speaks about Meter without being asked, and every space with Meter hardware still installed, fuel our growth.

sections.title: What Your Day-to-Day Will Look Like
paras: You manage a high-volume book of accounts across a range of sizes and verticals. In a given week, you will:
bullets: Kick off a relationship with a new 24/7 logistics customer, setting clear expectations for a successful partnership with Meter. Align on maintenance windows, hardware upgrades and change freezes during peak season.

Run dashboard walkthroughs with IT administrators at schools who recently switched to Meter. Based on their feedback, partner with Marketing to build a series of “back-to-school” webinars for school customers.
Partner with Meter Support to build a standard playbook for common non-technical customer tickets, from billing and circuit upgrade questions to move requests.

Audit accounts that have been quiet and determine what action, if any, is needed. Schedule in-person QBRs for a subset of these accounts, while reviewing support activity and other signals to assess sentiment across the rest.
Review expansion signals (e.g. headcount growth, leasing activity) across your book and proactively engage to discuss connectivity needs before new leases are finalized.
Debrief a support escalation with the engineering team, translating a recurring customer pain point into a scoped, actionable feature request.

sections.title: Who You Are
paras: This role is not a fit for someone who wants to manage a small number of high-complexity accounts, or who is only motivated by commercial deal-making. You care about whether Meter wins, not just whether your accounts are healthy. The operational challenges genuinely interest you: What does enabling independence for customers look like? How do you balance speed, quality, and scale? How do you measure success?

You know how to communicate, pay close attention to details, and want to own the outcome. Your customer-facing instincts are strong, and you know how to read what someone actually needs, not just what they are asking for.
This is a hybrid role in San Francisco or New York City.

Clinicians walk into appointments with the full patient picture already in hand, and that speed can mean spotting a condition early enough to actually treat it.

ashby:openrouter:3c898169-0219-4214-9c4c.summary:
OpenRouter is the leading AI routing and infrastructure layer that developers and enterprises use to access, manage, and optimize their AI use across models and providers. We help our customers avoid lock-in, capacity constraints, and unnecessary cost, giving them the flexibility to move fast, scale confidently, and adapt as models evolve.

OpenRouter sits at the center of how developers and organizations discover, evaluate, integrate, and operate the world’s leading open and proprietary models, routing billions of tokens across dozens of model labs and inference providers every day.

sections.title: About the Role
paras: We’re hiring a Product Manager for OpenRouter’s marketplace between developers and inference providers. We need your help as we transform our routing layer into a liquid marketplace that raises the quality floor for the entire ecosystem and opens up new ways to buy and sell inference.

You’ll drive the marketplace mechanics, provider-facing products, and economic incentives that match supply and demand. Alongside the engineering, operations, and partnerships teams, you’ll launch new market structures (like auctions, priority lanes, and dynamic pricing), build the benchmarks and diagnostics that help providers compete for traffic, and turn manual onboarding and operations into self-serve APIs. The features you’ll launch will impact the entire inference ecosystem.

This role is for a technical product builder who thinks in market incentives, unit economics, and distributed systems, and who works shoulder-to-shoulder with engineers to ship clean, durable infrastructure.

sections.title: What You’ll Do
bullets: Own the Provider Marketplace roadmap, from the provider dashboard, self-serve APIs, and onboarding pipelines to the prioritization, pricing, and quality mechanisms that govern traffic across the network.
Launch new market primitives. Design, test, and scale new ways to match inference supply and demand, including auctions, committed capacity, and dynamic pricing.
Shape the buyer and provider product experience. Build the demand-side buying controls and supply-side capacity tools required to make new markets liquid and easy to adopt.

Define inference prioritization and service tiers. Structure priority lanes, dedicated enterprise capacity, and flex tiers across customer reliability, provider margins, and OpenRouter’s business model.

Raise the provider quality floor. Build automated feedback loops (continuous evaluations, routing scorecards, and real-time failure diagnostics) so providers see why they win or lose traffic and fix regressions without filing a ticket.

Scale supply through self-serve product. Partner with Engineering, Provider Development, and Provider Operations to turn manual onboarding, model staging, pricing updates, and health checks into self-serve APIs.

Run the marketplace on data. Dig into request logs, routing metrics, and unit economics to find unmet demand, stranded capacity, or broken incentives, and turn those findings into crisp specs and shipped product.

sections.title: What We’re Looking For
bullets: 5+ years of product management, technical founder, or marketplace systems experience building products where algorithmic decision-making, economics, and infrastructure meet.

Experience on a two-sided marketplace, exchange, or price matching engine. You have worked on a scaled marketplace (such as commerce seller ecosystems, cloud compute markets, ad exchanges, or logistics marketplaces) and understand liquidity, price discovery, supply-demand balancing, and trust systems.

Technical background and engineering partnership. You have prior software engineering experience, studied Computer Science, or have equivalent technical depth. You understand API design, how to design around engineering constraints, and partner closely with engineers to scope, sequence, and ship complex projects iteratively.

Fluency with LLM inference stacks. You understand what happens when an inference request hits a provider (such as caching behavior, batching, and quantization decisions that drive cost vs. performance tradeoffs) so you can hold your own with lab and inference provider engineers.
Hands-on builder with code, data, and AI agents. You use coding agents daily to analyze data, prototype workflows, and validate specs before asking for engineering time.

Strong commercial and economic instincts. You enjoy digging into how each layer of the inference stack makes money. You know how to modeling margin and capacity tradeoffs, while designing incentives where customers, providers, and the platform all win.
High agency, velocity, and written clarity. You turn messy technical and economic problems into clear written strategies, talk directly to users and partners, cut scope intelligently, and ship fast.

sections.title: Nice to Have
paras: If you don’t think you meet all of the criteria above but are still interested in the job, please apply. Nobody checks every box, and we’re looking for someone excited to join the team.
bullets: Background at an inference provider, AI lab, neo-cloud, or GPU cloud, or building infrastructure for model serving and routing.
Hands-on work designing auction mechanisms, spot or batch compute markets, SLA tiers, or dynamic pricing models.
Track record building B2B seller or partner tooling, self-serve onboarding funnels, and partner analytics dashboards.

Year one: marketing is a predictable pipeline channel with its own number, every customer and dead deal in our database is in a motion, the proof library covers every product and vertical, and the CEO has not written a case study, built a sequence, directed a website page, or chased an event follow up in six months.

greenhouse:amperity:8249900.summary:
Most customer data is a lie by omission.

Every consumer brand wants to know its customers. Unfortunately, almost none actually do. Data is scattered across a dozen systems, half of it contradicts the other half, and "insights" teams are forced to act on incomplete guesses. We started Amperity ten years ago because that gap—between what a brand believes about its customers and what is true—is the most expensive problem in the industry, and nobody had solved it.

With a lot of hard work and a little bit of luck, we did. Our patented identity resolution takes billions of messy, conflicting records and resolves them into an accurate picture of a real human being—in hours, not months. That’s not a feature; it’s the foundation everything else stands on. It’s why more than 400 brands —like Alaska Airlines, Wyndham Hotels & Resorts, DICK’S Sporting Goods, Virgin Atlantic, and Brooks…

sections.title: About Amperity—Why This, Why Now
paras: Now we’re doing something harder. We’re rebuilding Amperity as an AI-first company—not bolting a chatbot onto old software, but putting agents at the center of how customer data actually gets used. We shipped the industry’s first identity resolution agent, then the first enterprise Customer Data Agent that turns a plain-language question into a live segment without waiting on an engineering queue. The bet underneath all of it is simple, and we think it’s correct: The potential of AI will not be realized for a brand until it’s grounded and activated against a true, unified view of the customer. The market at-large is focused on intelligence, and we are focused on being the ones who can make it trustworthy.

So here’s the honest pitch. If you want a tour of a category that’s already been figured out, this isn’t it. If you want to help decide what the next version of an entire industry looks like—alongside people who are remarkably exceptional at what they do, solving a problem that requires deep, sustained focus—this is one of the few places that work exists. Our goal is to build a highly impactful, generational business.
We measure our success by one standard: whether what we build moves the business. Return on cognition, not return on hype. If that’s how you want to be measured, we would love to speak with you.

sections.title: The Role
paras: At Amperity, the Director, Customer Value serves as the executive leader holding holistic commercial and strategic accountability for our entire Customer Success portfolio—spanning emerging $200K growth accounts to $4.5M+ multi-threaded strategic enterprises.

Reporting directly to CS Executive Leadership, you will establish the operational strategy, organizational design, and commercial architecture across all customer pods. You own aggregate Net Revenue Retention (NRR), Gross Retention (GRR), expansion pipeline, and customer health at the total book level. Rather than managing from a dashboard, you set company-wide standards for customer engagement, scale our operating models, and step in as executive sponsor on the highest-stakes commercial relationships.

You govern two distinct, harmonized operating models within a single organization: high-touch, bespoke coverage for enterprise strategic accounts, and a technology-enabled, instrumented system built for scale across high-volume tiers. You own the strategy, criteria, and governance that allow accounts to transition seamlessly between these tiers without friction, loss of value, or external handoffs.

sections.title: Responsibilities
bullets: Strategic & Commercial Book Ownership: Assume ultimate accountability for aggregate NRR, GRR, early renewal rates, and expansion pipeline generation across the total portfolio. Serve as the executive escalation point and executive sponsor on strategic, multi-million-dollar accounts.

Organizational Design & Resource Allocation: Lead the strategic design and resource deployment of customer pods. Optimize headcount allocation, pod alignment, and account load balancing as client complexity evolves. Partner with Pre-Sales and Sales Leadership to guarantee seamless, high-value handoffs at contract execution.

Dual Operating Model Strategy: Establish, refine, and enforce the operational frameworks for both high-touch strategic accounts (~$1M+ ARR) and scalable high-volume segments. Define the business logic, operational triggers, and governance models for accounts moving across tiers within your organization.

Operational Excellence & The Amperity Way: Codify, champion, and operationalize "The Amperity Way" customer engagement methodology. Model executive-level standard-setting through direct involvement in strategic account reviews, executive briefings (EBCs), and leadership coaching sessions.

Talent Architecture & Organizational Leadership: Build, lead, and develop a multi-tiered organization of managers, team leads, Senior CSMs, and Value Consultants. Establish hiring standards, performance management, succession planning, and promotion pathways to foster a high-performance talent bench.

Executive Cross-Functional Partnership: Act as the primary interface representing the Success organization to C-suite leadership, Sales, Product, and Engineering. Influence product roadmap priorities based on portfolio trends, systemic risks, and enterprise expansion opportunities.

sections.title: Interesting Problems
bullets: Architecting Smooth Tier Progression: Designing the quantitative criteria, workflow triggers, and team alignment needed to move scaling accounts into higher-touch operating models smoothly—ensuring account growth feels like an organic partnership milestone rather than a disruptive handoff.

Scaling AI-Driven Customer Operations: Championing AI fluency and automated intelligence systems across the team to multiply pod efficiency and shift proactive insight delivery onto AI-first platforms.

greenhouse:catonetworks:5015033101.summary:
Cato Networks is the converged network and security cloud for the AI era.

As AI reshapes cybersecurity, enterprises face a dual challenge: unlocking AI’s potential while defending against AI-driven attacks. Cato addresses both through a unified, cloud-native platform, providing the visibility and context to prioritize risks and stop threats in real time across users, applications, data, and AI agents.

Join us as we scale: take on ambitious technological challenges and shape the next generation of enterprise security at a company trusted by thousands of organizations worldwide.

sections.title: About the role
paras: Cato Networks is looking for a Product Marketing Manager to help customers understand the value of our Security Service Edge (SSE) offering within the broader Secure Access Service Edge (SASE) platform.

You will lead global product marketing initiatives for SSE, translating technical capabilities into clear positioning, differentiated messaging, and compelling customer stories. Working across Product, Sales, Sales Engineering, and Marketing, you will help bring new capabilities to market, equip the field to communicate their value, and build customer understanding and demand.

You will also support selected sales opportunities in Western North America by joining customer calls, delivering product and business-value messaging, and helping teams address buyer questions and competitive objections. Sales Engineering will provide technical discovery, solution design, and evaluation support.
bullets: Positioning and messaging: Develop clear, differentiated SSE messaging that connects Cato’s capabilities to customer challenges, buying priorities, and business outcomes. Tailor the story for security leaders, technical evaluators, and business stakeholders.

Product launches: Lead product marketing for priority SSE launches, aligning audiences, messaging, content, and field readiness across teams. Define launch objectives and assess results with your cross-functional partners.

Content and thought leadership: Create presentations, blogs, white papers, eBooks, webinars, and other assets that explain complex security topics, support buying decisions, and contribute to demand generation.

Competitive insight: Translate market research, customer feedback, and competitive analysis into differentiated messaging, practical battle cards, and guidance sellers can use in customer conversations.

Sales and partner enablement: Equip global sales, sales engineering, and partner teams with messaging, presentations, training, and objection-handling resources. Build their ability to explain Cato’s SSE value consistently and effectively.

Regional sales support: Partner with sales teams on selected strategic opportunities in Western North America. Join sales calls, deliver the SSE story, connect capabilities to customer priorities, and support deal progression alongside the assigned SE.
Customer and market feedback: Turn insights from customer conversations, sales engagements, and market research into recommendations for messaging, content, launch plans, and product priorities.
Cross-functional execution: Work with Product Management and Marketing on customer stories, events, campaigns, and analyst briefings, ensuring a consistent SSE narrative across channels.

sections.title: Qualifications
paras: A reasonable estimate of the salary for this role, at the time of posting, is $190,000 - $210,000. Cato operates from a high place of trust and transparency; we are happy to state the pay range for our open roles to best align with your needs. Exact compensation may vary based on skill set, experience, location, training, and certifications.
bullets: 4+ years of product marketing experience in cybersecurity, with demonstrated contributions to positioning, launches, content, and sales enablement.
Strong technical fluency in security and networking, with the ability to understand SSE capabilities and explain their relevance to customer needs.
Demonstrated ability to translate complex technical concepts into clear business value for both technical and executive audiences.
Strong writing and presentation skills, supported by examples of customer-facing content, presentations, or enablement materials.
Experience collaborating with Product Management, Sales, Sales Engineering, and Marketing to deliver shared priorities.
Ability to use customer research, competitive intelligence, and performance data to improve messaging and marketing decisions.
Strong prioritization and project management skills, with the ability to manage multiple initiatives across a global team.
An engineering degree or equivalent hands-on experience in cybersecurity, networking, or a related technical field.

greenhouse:celonis:7800529003.summary: Celonis is the trusted platform to industrialize Enterprise AI. At our core is the Celonis Context Model — which combines process data, business knowledge, and intelligence into a living digital twin of the enterprise that AI can actually understand, turning AI's operational blind spots into operational clarity. World's leading companies trust Celonis and its global ecosystem of partners to make their AI agents, people, systems, and processes work together, achieving transformational outcomes. We believe there's a massive opportunity to unlock global productivity and sustainability by giving AI the context to understand how every business process really works. Join our mission to make processes work for people, companies, and the planet.

sections.title: Role Description
paras: As a Lead Value Engineer specializing in the Life Sciences, you are pushing the envelope in solving business-critical problems for the world's largest, most diversified life science organizations. You will be working intimately with this strategic client, understanding their uniquely complex objectives—spanning from logistics to the precision distribution of advanced products—and building Celonis solutions using the world’s leading Process Intelligence (PI) platform in combination with top AI and ML technology partners (e.g., Microsoft, OpenAI, Databricks)..

With Celonis’ Process Intelligence (PI) platform, we feed operational context to AI so it understands the intricate realities of our customers’ business operations and enables them to industrialize AI. This unlocks real ROI on AI deployments at scale, ensuring life-saving products reach patients faster and safer. There is no AI without PI. You will prototype these solutions, demonstrate their value to customer business and IT leadership, and drive value realization to increase the footprint of Celonis across the healthcare and life sciences sector.

sections.title: Key Responsibilities
paras: Predictive Modeling and Optimization: Leverage data stored within the Celonis context model to design and deploy advanced time-series forecasting, optimization, and predictive algorithms to solve complex logistics constraints (e.g., dynamic inventory routing, schedule optimization).
bullets: AI Discovery & Solutioning: Understand the client's overarching AI strategy and the distinct challenges that are distinct to their business. As a Celonis product expert, translate these complex, multi-tiered requirements into innovative AI solutions that drive measurable impact..

Pre- and Post-Sales Execution: Actively drive the full customer lifecycle. Lead technical discovery and capability demonstrations during the pre-sales cycle, and remain deeply involved post-sale to guide implementation, ensuring agreed value and adoption thresholds in the supply chain are successfully reached.

Hackathons & Prototyping: Think out of the box, have a „can-do“ attitude, and don’t shy away from complex, fragmented supply chain networks. Leverage cutting-edge AI technologies to rapidly build creative prototypes in customer hackathons, solving critical pain points in planning, sourcing, manufacturing, and distribution.

Proof Projects: End-to-end execution of business-critical Proof-of-Value projects. This includes architecting and delivering secure, scalable LLM/agent systems with RAG, tools, and guardrails, while seamlessly integrating with enterprise systems of record.

sections.title: Requirements
bullets: 8+ years of experience leading technical pre-sales and post-sales engagements preferred within Healthcare, Life Sciences, Pharmaceutical, or MedTech. This includes defining AI roadmaps, building compelling ROI/TCO business cases, and guiding technical implementations through to value realization.

Expertise in generative AI techniques like RAG, few-shot learning, prompt engineering, multi-agent orchestration, multimodal understanding, or fine-tuning used to build high-impact use cases (e.g., intelligent chatbots for supplier collaboration, automated extraction of data from complex customs or quality documents).

Solid knowledge of Python and Advanced Predictive Analytic techniques (such as LangChain, pandas, pydantic, sklearn, PyTorch) as well as data engineering tools and technologies for leveraging massive, siloed datasets to build algorithms and tools aimed at predicting future business outcomes.

Strong presentation skills to both internal and external stakeholders (including supply chain executives and IT leaders), whether leading technical whiteboarding sessions or formal readouts and demos.
Bachelor’s Degree required; Master's Degree in computer science, supply chain management, engineering, mathematics, or related fields, or equivalent work experience preferred.

sections.title: Nice to Have (Big Plus)
paras:
Visa sponsorship is not offered for this role.

Onsite Requirement: This role will be expected to spend the majority of their time in the field meeting with clients.

Learn More about Value Engineering at Celonis Here
bullets: Hands-on experience building agentic systems using LLM orchestration, RAG, function calling, and prompt engineering, while ensuring safety through rigorous evaluations suited for highly regulated (GxP) life sciences environments.
Working knowledge of tools in the LLM ecosystem such as LangChain, LlamaIndex, or other OSS packages.
Experience in deploying and monitoring models at scale across major cloud platforms (AWS Bedrock, Azure AI, GCP Vertex).

greenhouse:ceribell:6251148004.summary: Ceribell is a medical technology company focused on transforming the diagnosis and management of patients with serious neurological conditions. The Ceribell System is a novel, point-of-care electroencephalography (“EEG”) platform specifically designed to address the unmet needs of patients in the acute care setting, and is being used in hundreds of community hospitals, large academic facilities and major IDN's across the country. Our entire team is driven by a shared commitment to transforming the landscape of critical care through our rapid seizure detection technology, come join the movement!

sections.title: Position Overview
paras: The Clinical Account Manager (CAM) is responsible for launching new hospitals and organic growth of install base of hospitals. The AM will also be responsible for providing on-going medical education to physicians and clinical staff using clinical information as the foundation for growth.
This Clinical Account Manager must be based within region, please no remote applicants. This role requires 60%/ 3 days a week travel.

sections.title: What You'll Do
bullets: Expand use of Ceribell to additional acute or critical care centers within existing customer base.
Work with the local Territory Manager to launch Ceribell at new customer sites.
Drive new product and technology introductions for existing customers.
Build advocacy and champions within facilities. Use hospital data to validate and build interest.
Develop a qualified lead funnel within existing install base. Regular activities consist of formal presentations, peer to peer education, new physician training, and driving physician education.
Responsible for upgrades and departmental expansion in existing install base.
Strong project management skill requirement to support new account launches.

Educate and train physicians, hospital personnel and/or office staff on the merits and proper clinical usage of company products. Become a clinical expert in use cases of Ceribell and relevant patient populations.

sections.title: What We're Looking For
paras: A candidate’s final salary offer will be based on their skills, education, work location and experience, and thus it may differ from the posted range. Compensation may also include bonuses consistent with Ceribell’s corporate compensation plan. Note, the above description is not all-encompassing and Ceribell reserves the right to change or modify job duties and assignments at any time.
bullets: 3-5 years of recent critical care sales experience OR 5 years of medical device or pharma sales experience OR RN’s with industry experience in supporting sales teams.
Excellent Communicator, Relationship Builder, Creative & Effective Problem Solver, highly organized and ability to prioritize strategically.
Ability to accurately assess and understand different stakeholders needs/wants. Process cross functional agendas and adjust strategy to achieve desired outcomes.
Confidence and expertise required to effectively challenge the status quo and influence meaningful change through consensus building
Driven & Coachable: innate desire to succeed; willing to seek out coaching, accept feedback and apply new skills supports measurable change
Grit, high integrity
Bonus points: start-up experience or experience working with disruptive technology, med device experience, neuro ICU clinical experience, sales experience.

greenhouse:chime:8943054002.summary: You'll join Chime's Growth Product Marketing team as the embedded growth owner for key parts of the consumer member funnel. You'll sit at the intersection of growth strategy, experimentation, performance analysis and product marketing craft: finding opportunities, running experiments and moving metrics against clear goals. You'll keep the core product marketing strengths of research, positioning and messaging, and go further by owning results and tradeoffs. Your work directly shapes how people find, join and start banking with Chime.

sections.title: In this role, you can expect to
bullets: You'll own growth strategy and outcomes for your part of the member funnel, from problem definition and opportunity sizing through roadmap delivery against quarterly and annual goals.
You'll be the embedded growth marketing lead in your squads, co-owning quarterly planning and roadmaps with Product, Engineering and Analytics.
You'll drive performance across acquisition, conversion, activation and early retention, with deep ownership of landing pages, enrollment flows and in-product onboarding.
You'll own the growth experimentation roadmap: set clear hypotheses and success criteria, then decide what to scale, iterate or sunset based on results.
You'll lead creative and messaging for experiments and launches across paid, lifecycle and owned surfaces, balancing speed, quality and compliance.

You'll own incentives, promotions and offers that drive qualified acquisition of primary banking relationships, balancing CAC, activation quality and long-term value, and partner with Lifecycle so acquisition, onboarding and retention feel like one journey.
You'll lead end-to-end GTM for your initiatives, track pacing against goals, and turn results into clear briefs and recommendations for Growth Marketing leadership.

sections.title: To thrive in this role, you have
paras: Below is the base salary offered for this role and level of experience. Full-time employees may also be eligible for bonus(es), competitive equity, and benefits. For commissioned roles, the base salary listed in this job description does not include incentive/variable pay. The actual base salary offered may be higher, depending on your location, skills, qualifications, and experience.
bullets: Deep experience in growth marketing, product marketing, performance marketing or a related role, including owning a funnel metric end to end and moving it.
A track record of driving measurable growth through experimentation and optimization, and the judgment to know when small optimizations have hit their limit and a bigger bet is needed.
Strong analytical skills: you define success metrics, diagnose funnel performance and pull out insights that change what the team does next.
Experience leading growth work through influence in a cross-functional squad, partnering closely with Product, Engineering and Analytics.
Sharp positioning and messaging craft, with examples of messaging changes that materially improved performance.
Clear storytelling and executive communication: you turn data into recommendations that leaders trust and act on.
Bonus: consumer fintech or other regulated-industry experience; familiarity with tools like Looker, Braze and web experimentation platforms.

greenhouse:clickstop:8645761002.summary:
Are you looking for an opportunity to be your best self while making a meaningful impact on the customer experience? Join our award-winning company and culture as a Customer Experience Specialist and help create exceptional experiences through problem solving, systems thinking, and customer advocacy.

“If you are ready to work in an environment where you are allowed the freedom and responsibility to act like an owner, and have a passion for helping customers, you won't regret joining Clickstop!” – Tammy, Current Employee

greenhouse:codeforamerica:8010686.summary:
Code for America believes government can work for the people, by the people, in the new digital age, and that government at all levels can and should work well for all people. For more than a decade, we’ve worked to show that with the mindful use of technology, we can break down barriers, meet community needs, and find real solutions.

Our employees build and transform government and community tools and services, making them so good they inspire change. We merge the best parts of technology, nonprofit, and government to help support the people who need it most.

With a focus on transparency and fairness, and deep empathy for partners in government and community organizations and the people that our partners serve, we’re building a movement of motivated change agents driven by meaningful results and lasting impact.

sections.title: About the role:
paras: In this role, you’ll work with a team of designers, researchers, engineers, product managers, and policy experts across our program portfolios. You will spend time with key government agencies to build rapport with their technical team, understand their technical needs, and develop a shared understanding of how Code for America can help them achieve their goals. This will involve identifying, designing, and building technical solutions to improve access to their programs.
Solutions Engineers at Code for America are an integral component of all of our program areas. There are currently three focused program areas at Code for America:
This role will report to the Solutions Engineering Manager and is expected to travel no more than 10% of the time.
bullets: Criminal Justice, which focuses on Automatic Record Clearance ,
Tax Benefits, which focuses on free trustworthy tax services and simplified tax filing ,
And the Social Safety Net . Focus areas in this portfolio include food benefits , integrated benefits applications , and training & capacity building .

sections.title: In this position you will:
bullets:
Partnerships and Collaboration


• Build and maintain relationships and develop technical champions within government and partner organizations.
Lead technical scoping for engagements, including project plans, statements of work, and technical requirements.

Work closely with cross-functional government partners to clarify problems and understand system constraints, and recommend feasible and high-value technical solutions that consider the needs of all stakeholders.
Document and communicate technical best practices to frame government RFPs.
Collaborate with government partners and provide written resources to communicate complex technical concepts.

Strategic Leadership


• Provide technical perspectives and expertise in service of improved government services for government agencies, organizational stakeholders, and other key audiences.
Estimate project scope and rough project plans for government initiatives.
Lead technical assessments of prospective new state engagements, including landscape research and partner capacity findings, and make recommendations that support team and leadership decision-making.

sections.title: About you:
paras: This role may be perfect for you if you have the technical skills to tackle engineering problems, the social skills to face human-factors problems, and the judgment to differentiate between the two. The ability to communicate complex technical concepts in straightforward language to non-technical audiences will be critical to your success. This is not a traditional sales engineering role – it’s a hands-on partner-facing engineering role where you'll use independent technical judgment with government partners and represent Code for America's technical approach.
bullets: 7+ years of experience as a Software Engineer, Solutions Engineer, or Solutions Architect with experience leading projects and interacting with customers.
Recent back-end development, database, data-science and/or devops experience.
4+ years of experience coding backend systems and data infrastructure in an industry-standard language (Python, Java, C#, Ruby, etc).
Recent experience integrating emerging technologies (e.g., generative AI models) into existing workflows or new solutions.
Strong self-management skills and a proven ability to manage multiple engagements simultaneously.
Fundamentally curious and empathetic; able to thoughtfully balance partner, user, and team needs and identify solutions that move the work forward towards greater impact.
Tenacity and adaptability; able to navigate relationships, ambiguity, and technical challenges and unblock yourself and your team.
Ability to engage in research to learn about current systems and architecture, and then incorporate this knowledge to design new solutions and new architectures.

sections.title: It’s a bonus if you have:
bullets: Experience working with or in government.
Personal experience with or professional experience working within the justice system, social safety net or other mission-relevant government services.
Experience working with machine learning or natural language processing technologies.
Experience with government procurement processes.
Active contribution to open source projects.

greenhouse:codepath:5161803007.summary:
CodePath is the largest educator of college computer science students in the country. We've trained over 50,000 students from more than 1,000 universities. Our partners include Amazon, Google, and other leading technology companies. After nearly a decade of training technical talent, we launched a $150M initiative with Anthropic to prepare people for careers in AI.

We're expanding into new markets and growing our team as AI changes the workforce. People joining CodePath now will help shape this next stage of our work.

We believe technical skills create opportunities. Our goal is to train millions of learners and create lasting economic impact. If you want to build something new, take ownership, and see the results of your work, this is a place to do it.

sections.title: Two things make this role unlike most PM jobs
paras: Learning rate is the scoreboard. Plenty of platforms can deliver content at scale. Almost none can prove their students learn faster because of them. You will be measured on outcomes, retention, and engagement, not feature velocity.

The ceiling is enormous. Every course CodePath delivers, direct or through partners, rides on the platform experience you build. As we scale to an order of magnitude of more students, your decisions compound across every learner we will ever serve.

You are a PM who has owned products that learners or users depend on every day, and you know how to walk into something live and make it measurably better. You are deeply AI-Native and you believe great learning products are judged by what learners can do afterward.
bullets: Own the core learner platform experience across every segment: college CS students, alumni, working engineers, and students at partner institutions
Translate learning, retention, and engagement goals into a prioritized roadmap
Use AI across your entire workflow to compress weeks into days, raising the quality and the speed of what you ship
Own our AI-assisted learning experiences end to end, including taking the AI Tutor and AI Grader from prototype to product. These student-facing AI surfaces are yours, not shared
Decide where AI accelerates effectiveness, productivity, and scale, and where human connection is essential to maintain motivation, commitment, and progress
Collaborate with Curriculum, Learning, and Engineering: they own what is taught and how the classroom runs, you build the platform that powers live delivery and asynchronous engagement
Set a high bar for design quality and engaging interactions across every learner touchpoint
Define the metrics that prove learning rate, retention, and engagement are improving at scale, and design experiments, grounded in discovery with users, to test your biggest bets

greenhouse:coinbase:8259870.summary:
Ready to do the most impactful work of your career? At Coinbase , we are uncompromising on our mission to increase economic freedom. The bar is high, the environment is intense, and we like it that way. This isn't a place for complacency, it’s a place to be pushed past your perceived limits. If you're ready to build the future of finance alongside people who refuse to settle for "good enough," you belong here. Coinbase is a remote-first, but not remote-only company. Expect to get together quarterly for intense in-person working sessions called “surges.” Learn more about working at Coinbase .

The DeFi Borrow team within the Consumer & Business group empowers millions of customers to unlock liquidity from their crypto assets directly inside the Coinbase Consumer app. You'll own the end-to-end product experience for crypto-backed borrowing, bridging Coinbase's centralized platform with…

sections.title: What you'll do:
bullets: Own the DeFi Borrow product area end-to-end, from vision and strategy through execution, launch, and ongoing iteration across web and mobile.
Drive the multi-year roadmap for crypto-backed loans, spanning initial borrow flows, advanced loan management, refinancing, and new product surfaces.
Define OKRs across workstreams (loan origination, positions management, liquidation, observability) and lead cross-functional teams to deliver against them.
Partner with Engineering to ship resilient, scalable borrowing experiences, balancing speed, safety, and reliability across core loan workflows, state tracking, and liquidation monitoring.
Collaborate with Risk, Compliance, Legal, and Finance to ensure products meet regulatory and controls expectations while preserving an excellent customer experience.
Build operational rigor through launch runbooks, on-call preparedness, degraded-UI strategies, and incident playbooks that keep DeFi Borrow reliable during market volatility.

sections.title: Required Skills and Experience:
paras: Pay Transparency Notice: Base salary varies by location (see range below). Total compensation may also include equity and bonus eligibility, and benefits (medical, dental, vision, 401(k)).
bullets: 5+ years of Product Management experience shipping consumer or prosumer financial products at scale, including at least one lending, credit, or collateralized product (e.g., margin, secured loans, DeFi borrowing).
Demonstrated ability to define and drive multi-quarter strategy, translate it into roadmaps and experiments, and deliver measurable results against growth and portfolio-health goals.
Familiarity with onchain concepts, smart contracts, and DeFi lending protocols (e.g., Morpho, Aave, Compound) sufficient to partner effectively with engineers on integrations and loan workflows.

Proven track record of using quantitative analysis (funnels, cohort behavior, risk/return tradeoffs) to inform product decisions and simplify complex financial concepts into clear, trustworthy consumer experiences.
Utilizes generative AI responsibly, maintaining human oversight to deliver business-ready outputs and drive measurable improvements in workflow efficiency, cost, and quality.

US Applicants: View Employee Rights , Know Your Rights , and E-Verify Notice of Participation.

greenhouse:constantcontact:8255896.summary:
At Constant Contact, we are seriously awesome people who take ownership and make an impact by operating with the mindset, integrity and courage of a small business owner. There’s something so profoundly rewarding about knowing that your work is empowering people everywhere to pursue their dreams . Here, we all play an integral part in helping business owners, entrepreneurs, non-profits and individuals to succeed by giving them all the help and tools they need to grow online. We’re energized by new challenges and new possibilities-and we’re just getting started!

We have an opening for a Principal Product Manager who will shape and grow Constant Contact's partner ecosystem through product innovation and strategy. This is not a Sales or Business Development role; you'll strategically define the product playbook for strategic partners, prioritizing integrations and experiences that reduce…

sections.title: What you’ll do:
bullets: Own the product strategy, roadmap, and launch of partner-driven experiences across multiple industry verticals

Build a reusable playbook: define how we identify, validate, and scale strategic partnerships, and which product solutions and experiences carry over from one partner to the next so Sales has a common approach that reduces one-off work and delivers a consistent user experience.

Define and ship integrations, embedded experiences, co-built offers, templates, and marketplace listings with partners including platforms, industry associations, networks and franchises, agencies, resellers, ecommerce providers, and AI companies
Work with engineering on APIs, data flows, authentication, and integration quality, including reliability, security, and ongoing maintenance
Identify where AI can speed up partner and customer onboarding, content creation, and automation, and prioritize it with engineering and design
Run discovery with partners and customers, then turn it into a clear roadmap and prioritized backlog
Design and run pilots with defined success criteria, then make scale, change, or stop decisions based on the data
Set and track the metrics for each partner product, including partner-sourced accounts, activation, attach rate, retention, expansion, ASP, and revenue

sections.title: Who you are:
bullets: 8+ years in product management , ideally in B2B, SaaS, platform, marketplace, or partner-integration products. We care more about what you’ve shipped and learned than about years or titles
Vertical SaaS or industry-specific partnership experience ( for example, Real Estate, financial services, or home services) is required
Experience taking a product from an unclear problem through validation, MVP, and launch, ideally with an external partner or integration
Comfort discussing APIs, integrations, data models, and system design with engineers, and writing clear technical requirements
Must have experience with rev-share, co-sell, or embedded distribution models
Experience linking product work to business results such as acquisition, revenue, attach rate, or retention
Experience turning customer and market insight into product decisions, ideally for small business or vertical audiences
Track record of leading cross-functional work and driving results through influence

sections.title: How we work:
paras: Constant Contact combines the strengths of an established company with the pace of a startup. We have 30 years of customer trust, a large base of small businesses, and the resources to back good ideas. On the B2B team, you’ll get the speed and freedom to use them.
bullets: Initiative is expected and rewarded. You’ll have room to identify opportunities, propose new approaches, and carry them through without waiting for a long approval chain.
Invention and reinvention are part of the job. You’ll build new products and also rethink how we approach partnerships, from process to packaging.
Small, fast cycles. We favor quick pilots, clear success criteria, and decisions based on results.
Scale behind you. You can use the company’s customers, data, brand, and cross-functional experts to make a new idea work faster than a startup could.

sections.title: How we’ll measure success:
paras: The specific salary offered to a candidate may be influenced by a variety of factors including the candidate’s experience, their education and work location. In addition, some roles may be eligible for additional on target commission pay or bonus. The compensation package includes health and welfare benefits including paid leave.
bullets: Multiple partner experiences launched, each with measurable growth in new accounts and revenue
A documented, repeatable playbook tested across more than one vertical and market
Evidence-based decisions on which verticals to scale, adjust, or stop
A prioritized pipeline of next opportunities, backed by market and customer evidence

greenhouse:databricks:8824166002.summary: The Public Sector Field Enablement Manager builds the enablement strategy that helps Databricks win new public sector customers, deepen account engagement, and grow platform consumption with a focus on Federal and National Security. This role partners with Sales and Field Engineering leadership to translate public sector priorities into measurable improvements in field readiness, pipeline, ramp, and consumption outcomes.

sections.title: The Impact You Will Have
bullets: Within the first 12–18 months, establish a prioritized public sector enablement roadmap supporting approximately 75 account executives and the field engineers aligned to their accounts, with progress and business impact reviewed in regular leadership business reviews.
Improve public sector field readiness by establishing and increasing adoption of role-specific certifications, skills, and selling behaviors for account executives and solutions architects.

Reduce time to productivity for new public sector account executives and solutions architects by establishing repeatable ramp outcomes tied to procurement, compliance, buyer, and Databricks platform knowledge.

Increase enablement-influenced pipeline and public sector consumption attainment by equipping field teams to apply segment-specific account strategies, value narratives, and sales plays in active opportunities.
Improve deal execution in public sector accounts by enabling teams to navigate government procurement vehicles, security requirements, compliance considerations, and competitive positioning.

Create a measurable feedback loop between the public sector field, business unit leadership, GTM & support teams, and Global Enablement that converts recurring field needs into prioritized programs and scales successful practices into broader enablement motions.

sections.title: What We Look For
bullets: 6+ years of experience in sales enablement, revenue enablement, field enablement, sales, or technical pre-sales within the technology sector, including experience supporting both commercial and technical audiences.

Demonstrated experience supporting, selling to, or enabling teams that serve federal or national security agencies , with a practical understanding of public sector procurement, compliance, and buyer decision-making.
Proven ability to build and operationalize an enablement function or major program from the ground up in a fast-moving environment.
Experience serving as a trusted advisor to senior Sales and Field Engineering leaders and translating business strategy into prioritized enablement outcomes.
Exceptional written, verbal, storytelling, and presentation skills, including the ability to influence executives and engage large audiences.
A measurement-oriented approach to enablement, with experience connecting readiness, skills, and behaviors to pipeline, consumption, ramp, or other business outcomes.

Experience using AI technologies to create, scale, measure, or deliver enablement, along with the ability to build working knowledge of data and AI concepts, Lakehouse architecture, and the Databricks platform.

The pay range(s) for this role is listed below and represents the expected base salary range for non-commissionable roles or on-target earnings for commissionable roles. sections.title: About Databricks

We operate at a global scale and are looking for practical problem solvers who thrive on real-world challenges and rapid growth. This is a senior individual contributor role with the independence to set direction and the accountability to deliver it. You will mobilize teams across Zipline, resolve the hardest questions standing between market opportunity and customer launch, and carry the plan through to stable operations. You will also build the metro-entry playbook that local leaders can adapt and every future launch can build on.

sections.title: What You'll Do

Design the entry network with Network Planning and Real Estate: first-wave sites, coverage, connectivity, maintenance support, and expansion waves. Preserve alternatives and redirect effort as jurisdictions or site opportunities change.

Shape the go-to-market with central and local commercial leaders and their restaurant, enterprise, and strategic partners. Define launch selection, customer coverage, and success measures; partner with Communications and Marketing on a launch approach grounded in actual readiness.

Drive the metro critical path across development, construction, hiring, fleet, maintenance, flight operations, and marketplace readiness. Resolve tradeoffs, secure functional commitments and approvals, and lead readiness reviews through go-live and operational handoff, while Site and Partner Launch own detailed execution.

Recommend which construction-ready sites come off the bench through Launch Activation Reviews, securing approval and placing sites into launch quarters. Keep activation decisions separate from customer-launch clearance.

Steward the pipeline-based projected network until Network Planning is staffed. Show where we could launch without implying commitment, and turn the strongest options into actionable launch recommendations.

Own and evolve the metro launch playbook. Establish entry principles and readiness gates, test launch hypotheses, and use early customer, partner, and operating results to improve subsequent waves and future metros.

The leadership to align senior stakeholders, make sound tradeoffs, and turn competing priorities into decisions and action without formal authority.
Commercial and product judgment, backed by hands-on analysis. You can build useful models with imperfect data; spreadsheet fluency is expected, with SQL, geospatial analysis, or scripting a plus.
Clear communication and a builder’s instinct: you create playbooks and operating mechanisms that others can use, not processes that depend on you.
Willingness to travel and learn directly from markets, partners, and field teams. Experience with regulated operations, infrastructure, autonomous systems, or real estate development is valuable.

sections.title: The role
paras: We are hiring our first product manager to work closely with our CPO, CTO, product operations manager, and engineering team. You will own improvements to how our firm delivers legal services: understand how our attorneys work, learn how our clients experience that work, and turn those insights into software improvements that ship.

We want someone with at least 3 years of product management experience and a strong record of delivering useful software. You should be comfortable getting into the details: watching a lawyer work, reproducing a bug, testing a prototype, writing a clear spec, and following through after launch. sections.title: What you will do
bullets: Work directly with our attorneys and clients to understand where our legal service breaks down, how our software contributes, and which improvements would make the biggest difference.
Turn interviews, support requests, usage data, and workflow observations into a prioritized backlog. Make clear tradeoffs between bugs, usability improvements, and new capabilities.
Own features from discovery through launch: define the problem, scope the solution, write requirements and acceptance criteria, and work with engineering through delivery.
Bring strong product and design judgment to complex workflows. Use wireframes or lightweight prototypes to test ideas and make the experience easier to understand.
Test what we build, catch edge cases, and coordinate releases. Follow up with users to confirm that the change solved the problem.

Measure whether changes improve our legal service: faster matter turnaround, less manual work for our attorneys, fewer client handoffs, and clearer communication. Use the results to decide what to improve next.
Keep our founders, engineers, product operations manager, and attorneys aligned on priorities and decisions. Bring enough structure to keep a small team moving quickly.

sections.title: What we are looking for
bullets: At least 3 years of product management experience building software with an engineering team. You can point to products or features you personally took from problem discovery to launch and explain the results.
Excellent product judgment. You can distinguish a recurring user problem from a one-off request, identify the smallest useful solution, and make hard prioritization calls.
A high bar for execution and quality. You take ownership, move quickly, notice details, and close the loop without needing someone else to chase the work.
Strong user research skills and empathy for people doing complicated work. You ask good questions, observe actual behavior, and turn what you learn into concrete decisions.
Clear writing and communication. Your specs are concise, your decisions are understandable, and you can work effectively with engineers, lawyers, and founders.
Technical fluency. You can discuss APIs, integrations, data flows, and AI product limitations with engineers. You do not need to be a software engineer.
Comfort with ambiguity and changing priorities at an early-stage company. You can make progress with incomplete information and update your view when the evidence changes.
